module_title: Net Concepts (NDP and NNP) and Depreciation
introduction: No machine, building, or asset remains brand new forever; its value decreases over time due to wear and tear. At this intermediate level, we will understand how to transition from 'Gross' values to 'Net' values by using the concept of 'Depreciation'.

core_concepts.title: Depreciation
core_concepts.description: During the production process, physical capital assets (like factory machinery, computers, and delivery trucks) suffer normal wear and tear or become obsolete. The monetary value of this loss in asset value over a year is called 'Depreciation'. In official terms, it is called the 'Consumption of Fixed Capital'.

core_concepts.title: NDP (Net Domestic Product)
core_concepts.description: When you subtract the value of depreciation from the Gross Domestic Product, you get the Net Domestic Product. (Formula: NDP = GDP - Depreciation). NDP will always be mathematically lower than GDP because depreciation can never be zero.

core_concepts.title: NNP (Net National Product)
core_concepts.description: When you subtract depreciation from the Gross National Product, you get the Net National Product. (Formula: NNP = GNP - Depreciation). NNP is considered the purest, most accurate evaluation of a nation's true economic output.

core_concepts.title: Significance of NDP
core_concepts.description: NDP is rarely used to compare economies globally because different countries have different rates of depreciation. Instead, economists use NDP domestically to understand how much of the country's capital stock is eroding and how much new investment (R&D) is needed just to maintain current production levels.

important_entities.name: Consumption of Fixed Capital
important_entities.significance: In official National Income Accounting documents and difficult UPSC/State PCS exam questions, the word 'Depreciation' is often deliberately hidden. Examiners will instead use the term 'Consumption of Fixed Capital' to trap students who only memorized the basic term.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Gross to Net Golden Rule
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Whenever you need to convert ANY 'Gross' economic aggregate into a 'Net' aggregate, the single and only operation you perform is subtracting Depreciation. (Gross - Depreciation = Net).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Drop the Wear to get the Net
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: GDP minus Wear & Tear (Depreciation) = NDP. GNP minus Wear & Tear (Depreciation) = NNP.

exam_strategy_tips: State PCS exams often ask for expanded formulas. Remember this chain: NNP = GDP + NFIA - Depreciation.
